{{Short description|Stream cipher}}
{{refimprove|date=February 2016}}
'''SOBER-128''' is a synchronous [[stream cipher]] designed by Hawkes and Rose (2003) and is a member of the [[SOBER (cipher)|SOBER]] family of [[cipher]]s. SOBER-128 was also designed to provide [[Message authentication code|MAC]] (message authentication code) functionality.

Watanabe and Furuya (2004) showed a weakness in the MAC generation of SOBER-128 which means an attack could forge a message with probability 2<sup>−6</sup>.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Watanabe |first1=Dai |last2=Furuya |first2=Soichi |title=A MAC forgery attack on SOBER-128 |url=https://www.iacr.org/archive/fse2004/30170472/30170472.pdf }}</ref> MAC functionality was deleted by Qualcomm from SOBER-128 reference code.

SOBER-128 takes a [[key (cryptography)|key]] up to 128 bits in length.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Hawkes |first1=Philip |last2=Paddon |first2=Michael |last3=Rose |first3=Gregory |title=Primitive Specification for SOBER-128 (Version 2.0) |url=https://opensource.qualcomm.com/assets/pdf/SOBER-128-v2.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402224226/https://opensource.qualcomm.com/assets/pdf/SOBER-128-v2.pdf |archive-date=2 April 2012 |page=3}}</ref>
